thread:
arpita_csm: Quick heads-up — NovaRetail onboarding: renewal touch in ~6w. Their search endpoint has 360ms p95 and token costs spiking. Thinking a controlled int8 quant swap + route split to compact model for low-latency paths. Any concerns?
ben_eng: +1 for int8 pilot. We should run a small canary on 5% traffic first. Need to confirm no accuracy regressions on their top 200 prompt set.
michaela_research: I can run the evals. Please share the top queries and expected intents. Also suggest we compare logits/ROUGE on the critical flows.
arpita_csm: Sent the sample set to you in this thread and uploaded to the onboarding bucket: https://internal.redwood/s/novaretail/onboard-samples :sparkles:
sam_ops: From infra side, if we do int8 we should enable fallback routing to the fp16 path for requests that exceed KV cache hit thresholds. Otherwise p95 might spike under burst.
ben_eng: Agree. Proposed rollout: canary (int8-quant-1) -> monitor quality and p95 for 24h -> 25% -> 50% -> full. Routing snippet for canary:
```yaml
routes:
 - match: latency_sensitive
   weight: 5
   model: novaretail-int8-v1
 - match: default
   weight: 95
   model: novaretail-fp16-v2
```
arpita_csm: Good. Can we add an automated regression alert tied to our eval suite? I want a Slack ping if top-intent accuracy drops >1.5%.
michaela_research: Will add a job. Also will produce a small diff report every 4 hours during canary with sample failures.
ops-bot: perf-alert: p95 for novaretail-search rose 12% at 10:12 UTC (detected). Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/novaretail/search
ben_eng: Thanks ops-bot. We'll hold canary until we confirm prefix caching parameters — ps: try increasing prefix_cache_size by 20% for the int8 ships.
sam_ops: I'll patch the runtime config and queue the canary start for 13:00 UTC. Assigning owners: ben_eng (rollout lead), michaela_research (eval), sam_ops (runtime), arpita_csm (customer comms).
arpita_csm: Great — I'll prep the renewal health note with expected cost savings (est ~18%) and timeline. Ping here once canary looks stable :thumbsup:
